title: Irreducible Combinatorially Symmetric Sign Patterns Requiring a Unique Inertia: the composite-cycle length lemma for a one-cycle underlying graph (Lemma 3.2)
author: Partha Rana and Sriparna Bandopadhyay
work: Irreducible Combinatorially Symmetric Sign Patterns Requiring a Unique Inertia
difficulty_reason: The counted lemma is the structural result on which the paper's cycle-containing half rests (the authors announce it at source0.tex line 1498 as the tool that determines the structures an irreducible combinatorially symmetric sign pattern with a 0-diagonal and a single cycle cannot have if it requires a unique inertia), and it carries the longest proof block of the paper, 118 lines, against 54 lines for Theorem 3.2 and 47 lines for Theorem 3.3. With the paper's definitions of the qualitative class, of combinatorially symmetric sign patterns with a 0-diagonal, of signed directed graphs, of composite cycles and of their length all supplied in the retained context, the proof still has to be built: it runs an induction on the number of leaves, constructs for the base case the maximum composite cycle \\bar\\Gamma = \\gamma\\gamma_1\\gamma_3\\cdots\\gamma_{2r-1} of D together with its counterpart \\Gamma in D\\setminus V(C), then splits the inductive step into the case where the neighbour v of a farthest leaf u is adjacent to more than one leaf and the case where it is adjacent to exactly one, in the second of which it must compare two maximum composite cycles \\Gamma_1 and \\Gamma_2, replace the edge (v_{2r},v) by (v,u), prove the identity l(\\Gamma_1') = k + l(\\Gamma_2'), draw and read two purpose-made graphs, and finally iterate an edge-deletion process whose invariant (fewer than t leaves with the distance to the cycle still even) has to be maintained. An ordinary PhD qualifying examination does not ask for this kind of induction over signed digraphs with a maximum-length invariant, so the unit is above the bar; the devices are however elementary graph-theoretic case analysis rather than deep machinery, so it is recorded as H2 rather than H3.
